A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPEC/SPEC-align work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 Section 6 and Appendix B report original embedding comparisons, clustering diagnostics, alignment experiments, and ImageNet classification results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds eigensolver timings, random Fourier feature sensitivity results, and an alternative alignment experiment.

M1.justification: v3 adds a Cholesky-based reduction to a symmetric eigenproblem (Remark 1 and Appendix A.3) and an eigenvalue-l2/Frobenius alignment objective with minibatch computation (Remark 2). These extend the computational procedure and alignment loss beyond v1. Algorithm 1 also corrects its symmetric-factorization expression and eigenpair indexing.

E1.justification: Both versions cover AFHQ, FFHQ, ImageNet-1K including ImageWoof and text-overlaid subsets, MS-COCO images and captions, GPT-4o-generated text, and WikiText-2. The new experiments vary computation and alignment within existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 introduces a runtime comparison between direct Algorithm 1/PyTorch eig and the Cholesky alternative. Existing embedding-model and classification comparators remain. The K-means agreement comparison on text-overlaid ImageNet disappears with Figure 3's diagnostic panels.

E3.justification: New experiments in v3 Appendix B.1 measure runtime across dimensions from 1,000 to 10,000 and sweep random Fourier features from 1,000 to 6,000, including paired visualizations at 2,000 and 6,000. Retained experiments preserve the default 2,000 features, bandwidth-selection rule, and fine-tuning configuration.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of eigensolver scalability, cluster sensitivity to the random-feature budget, and convergence under the alternative alignment loss (Appendices B.1 and B.6). Conversely, Figure 3 loses its UMAP, within-cluster-distance, and K-means agreement diagnostics. Earlier visualization-method ablations and similarity-ranking sanity checks remain.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose 50 K-means runs, retain the same AMI/NMI uncertainty-reporting practice, and specify training seed 0. v3 introduces no new repeated-run, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing procedure. The deleted Figure 3 statistics are removed results rather than a revised reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 Table 1 adds runtimes, including 72 seconds for direct computation versus 33 for Cholesky at d=4,000, and 85 seconds for Cholesky at d=10,000. Figures 6-9 add feature-budget-dependent cluster findings, and Figure 22 adds l2-alignment convergence results. Figure 3 loses four AMI results and associated diagnostics. Matched ImageNet accuracies remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds the Cholesky spectral-equivalence derivation and Frobenius-distance identity. It restores feature-dimension factors in the complexity analysis and changes Theorem 2's bound from 128 log(2/delta)/m to 128 log(3/delta)/m, correcting the exponential factor in its appendix proof. These are substantive mathematical additions and corrections.

C1.justification: The central contributions of interpretable embedding comparison, scalable computation, and alignment remain. The introduction refines the scalability claim from O(max{d^3,n}) to O(d^2 n+d^3), preserving linear dependence on sample size for bounded feature dimension.

C2.justification: v3 adds practical qualifications concerning low-feature-budget cluster inconsistencies and the scaling limits of direct eigendecomposition (Appendix B.1). Remark 2 explains the minibatch-optimization advantage of Frobenius alignment. Existing interpretations of embedding semantics and the limitation to spectrally detectable clusters largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 identifies PyTorch eig as the direct implementation used in the runtime comparison and replaces the abstract's direct code-repository pointer with a project-page pointer. Existing hardware information, synthetic-data prompt, and fine-tuning hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly positions SPEC as a kernel-PCA extension, contrasts it with Vargas et al. (2024), and acknowledges concurrent Frobenius alignment by Gong et al. (2025). It adds selected random-feature and generative-evaluation references while removing citations including Boggust et al. (2022) and Ng et al. (2001). The overall related-work scope remains similar.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify terminology, complexity, and matrix asymmetry. Remarks 1-2 and new appendix subsections expand the exposition, while the main section order and most existing experimental and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands visual presentation with feature-budget image grids, paired t-SNE/UMAP displays, an alignment-kernel and convergence figure, and a runtime table. Figure 3 is shortened by removing diagnostic panels. Existing configuration and accuracy tables move from v1 page 28 to v3 page 38; most other figures are retained with new numbering.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens technical reliability by correcting Algorithm 1's treatment of the nonsymmetric matrix, restoring feature-dimension factors in the scalability analysis, and repairing Theorem 2's bound. The Cholesky derivation, runtime measurements, and feature-budget sensitivity tests give the central scalability argument stronger practical support. These gains and the evaluated alignment alternative outweigh the loss of Figure 3's diagnostic evidence.
